questions.question: 3. What is needed to observe tiny details of a sample under an optical microscope

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option. While magnification enlarges the image, it does not reveal details beyond the microscope’s limit.
explanations.b: This is the correct option. Resolution determines the ability to distinguish two closely spaced points as separate, which is essential for observing fine details.
explanations.c: This is an incorrect option. Without sufficient resolution, high magnification will only produce a larger blurred image, not reveal tiny features.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option because observing fine details requires resolution.

questions.question: 4. Which of the following steps is not typically part of metallographic sample preparation for bright field microscopy?

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option because mounting provides mechanical support to small or fragile specimens during grinding, polishing, and etching.
explanations.b: This is an incorrect option because etching selectively attacks grain boundaries, phases, or defects to reveal the microstructure that is not visible on the polished surface.
explanations.c: This is a correct option. Staining with dyes is generally not used in metallography; it is more common in biological microscopy to enhance contrast in soft tissues or cells.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option because polishing produces a smooth, flat surface by removing scratches and damage from grinding, which is necessary before etching and microscopic examination.

questions.question: 5. In bright field microscopy of metals, etching is primarily used to:

answers.b: Improve the conductivity of the sample
answers.c: Enhance the visibility of microstructural features
answers.d: Increase the reflectivity of the sample surface

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option because etching does not remove or prevent oxidation.
explanations.b: This is an incorrect option because etching does not enhance the electrical conductivity of a metal.
explanations.c: This is the correct option. In bright field metallography, etching selectively attacks grain boundaries, phases, or defects, creating contrast that makes these features visible under the microscope.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option because etching actually reduces surface reflectivity in many cases.

questions.question: 6. In dark field microscopy of metal samples, which part of the light contributes to image formation?

answers.a: Reflected light from the sample surface
answers.b: Light directly transmitted through the sample
answers.c: Light scattered by surface features or defects

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option because in dark field microscopy, the directly reflected light is blocked from entering the objective.
explanations.b: This is an incorrect option because in dark field microscopy, the image is formed only by light scattered by features or defects, not by unscattered light passing straight through.
explanations.c: This is the correct option. In dark field microscopy, the microscope is configured so that only light scattered by the sample enters the objective lens.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option. Fluorescence is a separate imaging technique that requires a fluorescent sample and specific excitation light, which is not part of standard dark field microscopy.
